decisions.quote: Our direct replication of Mueller and Oppenheimer’s Study 1 showed that, relative to longhand note taking, laptop note taking boosted word count and verbatim overlap with lecture content, but it did not reduce knowledge of the lecture material after a brief delay with no opportunity to study. Results, thus, did not support the idea that longhand note taking improves performance via better encoding of information.
decisions.reason: Although the study replicated the differences in note word count and verbatim overlap, those measures test the proposed encoding mechanism underlying the central learning claim, and the authors' explicit inference criteria required significant effects on both note content and conceptual quiz performance for a successful replication. Across the Abstract, Statement of Relevance, and Conclusion, the authors state an overall verdict that their results do not support the claim that longhand note taking improves immediate learning via better encoding of information.
